newsitem.title: ITALY: Georgia's Shevardnadze makes two-day trip to Rome.
newsitem.headline: Georgia's Shevardnadze makes two-day trip to Rome.

text.p: President Eduard Shevardnadze arrived in Rome on Wednesday for the first official visit by a Georgian head of state since the days of ancient Roman Emperor Hadrian.
Shevardnazde, a former Soviet foreign minister, was due to meet leading Italian politicians and have an audience with Pope John Paul during the two-day trip.
Shevardnazde opened his visit with a meeting with Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and was due to address a business conference on the Georgian economy later on Wednesday.
He mets Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini on Thursday. His Papal audience is set for Friday morning, after which he flies home.

Shevardnazde, a key figure in five years of Soviet reform that helped end the Cold War, resigned as foreign minister in 1990. Georgia won independence from the Soviet Union in 1991 and Shevardnazde, 69, has been its leader since 1992, although he did not have the title of president at first.
He is the first Georgian leader to visit the Italian capital since Hadrian invited King Pharsman II nearly 2,000 years ago.
